note: Four phase safety, efficacy, effectiveness and monitoring model, a clean structure for staging a clinical AI rollout.
title: Clinical trials informed framework for real world clinical implementation and deployment of artificial intelligence applications
explain_beginner: Healthcare organizations are deploying artificial intelligence tools but lack clear guidance on doing so safely. This paper proposes a four-step framework borrowed from how medical treatments are tested in clinical trials. Organizations should first verify the AI system works correctly, then confirm it produces the intended results, then compare it against existing methods, and finally monitor its performance over time. This structured approach helps ensure AI in healthcare is reliable and benefits patients fairly.
explain_business: Organizations planning healthcare AI investments need a proven roadmap to reduce deployment risk and ensure adoption succeeds. This framework provides that roadmap by breaking implementation into four validated stages, similar to drug approval processes. Executives can use this structure to allocate resources appropriately, set realistic timelines, and demonstrate to stakeholders that deployments meet safety and effectiveness standards. Following this approach protects against costly failures and positions organizations to capture the full value of AI investments.
explain_practitioner: The authors present a four-phase implementation model for clinical AI deployment. Phase one validates safety, phase two demonstrates efficacy, phase three establishes effectiveness through comparison with existing standards, and phase four implements ongoing monitoring. This framework parallels established clinical trial methodology, providing implementers with a structured pathway from development to real-world use. The approach emphasizes institutional collaboration and seeking funding support to enable rigorous, systematic AI deployment that prioritizes patient outcomes and equitable access.
